thesis: A five-colour Dragon deck that buys its own curve down with five cost reducers, then multiplies each arrival twice over — once into more bodies and triggers, once into doubled damage — and whose kill is proven on a board and still unproven as a board it can reach.

stages.label: THE FIVE-COLOUR TOLL, NOW PAID IN CREATURES
stages.what_it_does:
Pays for a nine-mana commander and a Dragon top end out of 36 land copies (32 entries), four rocks, three land-fetching sorceries and — the v1.0.2 change — five mana CREATURES where artifacts used to be: Birds of Paradise, Bloom Tender, Delighted Halfling, Faeburrow Elder, Ignoble Hierarch. 44 cards, the largest stage by far. Mean available mana at turn five reads 5.934 against v1.0.0's 4.219, and 6.734 at six. 'Ramp or fixing drawn' is the deck's best-covered component at 0.904 assembled / 0.824 by turn six, mean turn 2.213. deck-audit prices the cost: 22 ramp copies against a 10-12 ratio, verdict 'over'.

Twelve of the 36 land copies enter tapped and only one always — exactly a third, where v1.0.0 ran 15 of 36 and mana_analysis's notes flagged it as over the one-in-three budget; that flag is gone. Colour is still uneven: on-curve from lands alone G 0.849, U 0.810, W 0.787, R 0.718, B 0.441 on 13 black land sources against a 30-source yardstick, lifted to 0.636 by rocks and dorks.

The cost of the fixing is LIFE and fragility. mana_analysis counts 8 life per tap-cycle recurring and 13 one-time on entry. The recurring 8 is six cards enumerated: Battlefield Forge, City of Brass, Mana Confluence, Shivan Reef and Spire of Industry at 1 each, Tarnished Citadel at 3 — and four of the six carry a free '{T}: Add {C}' mode, so the toll is paid only for colour. Gemstone Mine is three activations and then it is gone. Forbidden Orchard hands an opponent a 1/1 every time you tap it.

Two lands are not only mana: Cavern of Souls makes a Dragon spell paid with its mana uncounterable, and Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon sacrifices for a Dragon. Six sources are DRAGON- or LEGEND-restricted and deck-facts warns they pay for spells only, never a coloured activation.

evidence.note: all 15 members are lands and all 15 are here
all 17 members are lands and all 17 are here
all four members are the deck's rocks — Sol Ring, Arcane Signet, Chromatic Lantern, Dragon's Hoard
five of the eleven-card Ramp city are my mana dorks; the other six are Treasure Dragons I filed under fuel and wincon, so the map cannot tell a dork from a Dragon that makes Treasure
Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim say 'search your library', so the map files them beside Worldly Tutor and Enlightened Tutor; in this deck they are lands
8 cards carry it in the histogram, against 4 ramp:rock — the inversion v1.0.2 made

stages.label: THE PRICE CUT
stages.what_it_does:
What has to happen before the deck is doing its thing is that a Dragon becomes affordable ahead of curve, and half of it is true on turn one. Eminence works from the command zone: other Dragon spells cost {1} less with nothing to cast, nothing to resolve and nothing an opponent can remove. The other half is four printed reducers — Urza's Incubator {2}, Dragonspeaker Shaman {2}, Herald's Horn {1}, Dragonlord's Servant {1}. An oracle scan of all 96 entries for 'less to cast' returns exactly those four plus eminence.

Priced from the brief: a reducer drawn is 0.521 assembled, 0.422 by turn six, mean turn 3.264. At four cards that is 25.8% of opening sevens and 32.1% by turn three, against the cited yardstick that '5 copies is 31% of openers, 7 is 41%'. deck-audit does NOT flag it thin — it flags at 3 or fewer, and three components carry the flag: Dragon-restricted mana at 2, THE ENTRY KILL's damage leg at 3, THE COMBAT KILL's multiplier leg at 2. Reducer AND ramp together, the turn-five Ur-Dragon hand, is 0.463 / 0.336 at mean turn 4.195.

Sarkhan, Fireblood and Desolation of Smaug are a separate two-card component (0.302 / 0.234, thin) because their mana is spendable only on Dragon spells: manabase.land_colors scores restricted mana as zero sources, correct for colour maths and exactly wrong for 'can I cast a Dragon'. Desolation is also a one-sided sweeper.

The commander's BODY is not part of ignition in practice: mean cast turn 6.916, median 7, cast by turn six 0.329, and never cast by turn ten in 2,222 of 10,000 iterations — much improved on v1.0.0's 5,997 and still a fifth of games.

evidence.note: this stage's first claim is CHECKER-PASSED. 007 step 8 rules that a spell's total cost is locked in before any of it is paid, minus all cost reductions (601.2f), and that with The Ur-Dragon's eminence active FROM THE COMMAND ZONE Lathliss is paid for at {3}{R}{R} rather than her printed {4}{R}{R}.
five of my seven sit in the 13-card Insurance city — but so do five protection spells and three conversion cards, so one city holds three stages
Sarkhan, Fireblood and Desolation of Smaug file with the Dragons, because their loudest text is tokens and damage rather than the restricted mana they exist here to add
five cards carry it in the histogram; the fifth is the commander, whose eminence discount works from the command zone

stages.label: TREASURE, TUTORS AND TWO ENCHANTMENTS THAT COME BACK
stages.what_it_does:
What keeps the engine running once a Dragon has landed: Treasure, a specific Dragon on demand, and cards.

Five of the declared six Treasure sources are here — Atsushi, Goldspan Dragon, Old Gnawbone, Gadrak and Ganax; the sixth, Smaug the Magnificent, is under wincon because the Treasures it counts are the damage its own attack trigger deals. The group reads 0.676 assembled / 0.560 by turn six, mean turn 3.068. That drawn-rate is complete; every Treasure-derived MANA figure is a FLOOR, because meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled names THREE of the six (Atsushi, Gadrak, Ganax) — which is why the component's own label, 'the model can SPEND only two', no longer matches the file it is measured against. What the model does see is small: mean hoard 2.077 by turn ten, treasure engine online 0.155 by turn ten.

Two of the five are CONDITIONAL in a way the count hides. Atsushi's three Treasures are a DEATH trigger, and Gadrak makes one per nontoken creature that died this turn — in a deck with no sacrifice outlet at all (see absent_stages). Ganax is the unconditional one and is new in v1.0.2: a Treasure whenever Ganax or another Dragon you control enters, tokens included, which makes it the fuel side of the entry cascade.

Breaching and Roiling Dragonstorm each return to their owner's hand when a Dragon you control enters, which makes them recurring rather than one-shot — Roiling draws two and discards one, Breaching free-casts a nonland card of mana value 8 or less. That conversion-to-fuel loop is printed on the fuel, not on the payoff.

Finding a Dragon is two cards wide (Sarkhan's Triumph, Worldly Tutor) plus Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, filed in mana; Enlightened Tutor finds Panharmonicon or a Dragonstorm.

evidence.note: five of the eleven-card Ramp city are my five Treasure sources — the map groups them exactly as the declaration does — and the other six are mana dorks and Smaug, which I filed elsewhere
three of my tutors are here and the other three members of the Tutors city are the mana stage's land-ramp sorceries
Breaching and Roiling Dragonstorm file with the Dragons — the map hears the Dragon-typal trigger, not the cantrip that is the reason they are in the 99
six cards carry it, matching the declared component exactly

stages.label: ONE ARRIVAL BECOMES SEVERAL, AND EVERY POINT BECOMES TWO
stages.what_it_does:
The engine proper, and after v1.0.2 it has THREE families under one roof rather than two.

ENTRY. Miirym copies every other nontoken Dragon; Panharmonicon doubles every trigger an entering creature or artifact causes; Lathliss makes a 5/5 per nontoken Dragon; Ancient Gold Dragon rolls a d20 on combat damage; Utvara Hellkite makes a 6/6 per attacking Dragon; Sneak Attack puts one in from hand for {R}; Hellkite Courser is the only card in the 99 that puts a commander onto the battlefield from the command zone, and 005 refutes Sneak Attack doing it.

COMBAT. Atarka grants double strike to every attacking Dragon, Thrakkus doubles each Dragon's power, Radiant Destiny is a flat +1/+1, and Scourge of the Throne is the deck's only additional combat phase — it multiplies the combats rather than the damage inside one.

DAMAGE DOUBLING, NEW IN v1.0.2 AND THE REAL CHANGE TO THIS STAGE. Twinflame Tyrant doubles any damage a source you control would deal to an opponent or their permanents; Solphim doubles NONCOMBAT damage to the same targets. Both are replacement effects sitting behind the whole output stage, and neither is measured: the goldfish files Twinflame Tyrant and Solphim in THE COMBAT KILL's castable-DRAGON leg, as bodies, while its multiplier leg stays two cards and thin.

SPOF STAYS NULL, and 007 is why that needs an argument. Without Panharmonicon, 002's board falls from 64 damage to 20 and kills nobody. But Panharmonicon converts NOTHING alone — it doubles triggers other cards cause — while Miirym, Lathliss, Ancient Gold Dragon, Utvara Hellkite, Sneak Attack and Hellkite Courser each widen a board on their own printed text. 007 bounds one board's magnitude, not the stage's availability.

evidence.note: Panharmonicon doubles Miirym into two nonlegendary 6/6 Lathliss copies; the final state records that Lathliss's own trigger never fires, because every later entry is a token and both nontoken clauses exclude tokens
15 Faerie Dragon tokens enter as one event and Miirym copies none of them — a token is not a nontoken Dragon
Sneak Attack puts Drakuseth in with haste for {R}; the same stack refutes it reaching the command zone and names Hellkite Courser as the card that does

the counterfactual, and the argument behind single_point_of_failure staying null: 002's board with Panharmonicon removed and nothing else changed deals 20 in four instances instead of 64 in twelve. That is a bound on ONE BOARD'S MAGNITUDE. deck-audit's single_points_of_failure is empty and Panharmonicon sits in no goldfish component, so this null is judgement, stated as such.
ten of my thirteen sit in the 30-card Dragon city alongside all thirteen output cards; the map cannot separate a multiplier from a payoff, because both are printed in the same Dragon-typal words

THE SHARPEST DISAGREEMENT IN THIS ARTIFACT. Miirym, Solphim and Twinflame Tyrant file in the Insurance city beside the cost reducers and the protection spells, because their text reads as a condition on your own stuff. Two of the deck's three damage multipliers therefore share an address with Teferi's Protection.

stages.label: WHAT AN ARRIVAL IS WORTH
stages.what_it_does:
What the multiplied board produces, priced per entry rather than per turn.

DAMAGE. Dragon Tempest deals X to any target for each Dragon entering, where X is the Dragons you control; Terror of the Peaks deals that creature's power; Scourge of Valkas does Tempest's job on a 4/4 flying body and counts itself. Those three are THE ENTRY KILL's entire damage leg, thin at 3, and the target reads 0.235 assembled / 0.150 by turn six at mean turn 4.977. Firespitter Whelp deals damage too and is NOT in that leg, correctly: its trigger is on CASTING a noncreature or Dragon spell, not on a Dragon entering, and it hits each opponent for 1 rather than aiming X.

Stack 002 prices one Lathliss cast at 64 damage in twelve separately-targeted instances — 36 from Terror, 28 from Tempest — and 007 settles how that total may be spent: every instance reads 'any target', nothing forces them apart, and aimed at one seat the running total reaches 42 by the eighth, so a fresh 40-life seat dies. What neither board can do is kill two seats, 64 against 72.

CARDS. Temur Ascendancy draws on each power-4-or-greater arrival, Garruk's Uprising on the first and grants trample, Return of the Wildspeaker and Rishkar's Expertise cash the biggest body.

TARGETED ACTIONS. Swords to Plowshares, Generous Gift, Chaos Warp, Glorybringer's exert, and Crux of Fate — asymmetric by choice, though less so than it was. From the type lines: 22 of the 30 creatures in the 99 are Dragons, and the eight that are not are five mana creatures, two cost reducers and Solphim — so Crux of Fate's non-Dragon mode now costs you the whole acceleration package.

WHAT LEFT: Wrathful Red Dragon is out of the 99, and stack 004, which verified it, names a board this list cannot make. Nothing here cites it.

evidence.note: 64 damage across twelve instances: 36 Terror + 28 Tempest, with X = 4,4,5,5,5,5 at optimal trigger ordering
X is recomputed per trigger and every one of the fifteen sees 17 Dragons; Dragon Tempest is an Enchantment and does not count itself

resolution.final_state.summary clause (c), on how 002's total may be assigned: '002's "40-life opponent survives at 8" is an assignment choice, not a ceiling; what neither board can do is kill BOTH seats, since 64 < 72.'
all thirteen output cards sit in the 30-card Dragon city — the map agrees with this stage exactly and cannot separate it from conversion, which puts ten of its thirteen in the same place
seven cards carry it, which is how the taxonomy sees a payoff whose damage happens to be aimable at creatures

stages.label: THE TURN YOU MUST NOT LOSE
stages.what_it_does:
Six answers held out of the same open mana for the same turn — Teferi's Protection, Heroic Intervention, Flawless Maneuver, Boros Charm, Deflecting Swat and Lightning Greaves — measured 0.673 assembled / 0.565 by turn six at mean turn 2.959. That is the declared component exactly.

WHAT v1.0.2 TRADED, and it is not a like-for-like swap: three counterspells (Counterspell, Swan Song, Dovin's Veto) came out for Lightning Greaves. Greaves answers targeted removal at equip {0} and cannot answer a board wipe, which all three counterspells could; its shroud also stops YOUR own targeting. The group still reads 'protection held for the big turn' and that is the turn Greaves is for, but its coverage is narrower than the count suggests.

TWO OF THE SIX ARE PROBABLY NOT FREE HERE. Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat both read 'If you control a commander' — and The Ur-Dragon is a permanent only while it is on the battlefield. The goldfish casts the commander by turn six in 0.329 of runs at median turn 7, so on the turns this deck pivots these are often a {2}{W} and a {2}{R} spell. Two limits on that inference: the goldfish counts CASTS, not control, and Hellkite Courser is a second route onto the battlefield it does not model.

The measurable shape of the problem is interaction_castable_by_turn: 0.279 / 0.371 / 0.455 on turns four to six, and the model's own note calls that a FLOOR because it spends rather than holds.

THUNDERBREAK REGENT IS THE SEVENTH CARD AND SITS IN NO DECLARED PROTECTION COMPONENT — the goldfish files it in THE COMBAT KILL's castable-Dragon leg, as a body. It prices removal (3 damage to the player) rather than preventing it, so it belongs to the function of this stage and not to its measured rate.

evidence.note: five of my seven sit with the cost reducers and the two damage doublers in a 13-card city, because the map hears 'a condition on your own stuff' in a reducer and in Teferi's Protection alike
Deflecting Swat changes a target and Thunderbreak Regent is a Dragon body, so both file with the Dragons; the deck pays for the first five out of the same held mana on the same turn
seven cards carry it; the histogram splits the rest across protection:granted and protection:redirect, which is three names for one held-up turn

stages.label: PROVEN ON A BOARD, UNPROVEN AS A ROUTE
stages.what_it_does:
TWO OF THE FOUR PRESENTABLE PASSING STACKS ELIMINATE A PLAYER. 001 kills every opponent on its board; 002 kills the 32-life seat (704.5a); 005 deals 17. 007 settles 002 in both directions: without Panharmonicon the same board deals 20 and kills nobody, and on 002's own board the twelve instances may all be aimed at one seat, reaching 42 by the eighth — so a fresh 40-life seat dies. Neither board kills two seats, 64 against 72.

What is unproven is REACHABILITY against THREE seats at 40. 001 fixes its d20 at 15 for determinism and the kill does not need 15: the threshold is 12 or better, nine faces of twenty, and its precondition is that Ancient Gold Dragon has already connected in combat.

THE KILL MOSTLY DOES NOT LIVE IN THIS STAGE. It lives in OUTPUT — Dragon Tempest, Terror of the Peaks, Scourge of Valkas — declared as THE ENTRY KILL at 0.235 assembled / 0.150 by turn six, damage leg thin at 3. THE COMBAT KILL reads 0.243 / 0.157 at mean turn 4.866 with a multiplier leg thin at 2. Do not add the rates; the schema cannot express their union.

THIS STAGE IS NOW TWO CARDS. v1.0.2 removed both alternate finishers: Hellkite Tyrant, whose twenty-artifact upkeep clause was the deck's only alternate win, and Moltensteel Dragon. An oracle scan of all 96 entries for 'wins the game' / 'loses the game' now returns nothing. What is left is Drakuseth, which deals 10 on the attack before blockers and 7 in the air, and Smaug the Magnificent, which deals damage equal to your Treasures to any target and mints one per upkeep. Both are damage; the deck now has exactly one way to end a game.

evidence.note: its final_state kills both opponents on the board; the d20 threshold for three seats at 40 is 12 or better, not the 15 the scenario fixes
the second checker-passed elimination: 64 damage in twelve instances kills the 32-life seat under 704.5a and cannot kill the 40-life seat as well
Drakuseth's attack trigger is an attack trigger, not a cast trigger, so 4+3+3 fires the turn it arrives and all 17 damage stands after the mandatory sacrifice
Drakuseth files with every other Dragon; nothing in the map distinguishes a finisher from a body

Smaug the Magnificent files with the Treasure sources, which is also true — its own Treasure count is what its attack trigger deals, so it is simultaneously the fuel and the thing the fuel is spent on

absent_stages.why: RE-VERIFIED against the current 96 entries rather than carried forward. A regex scan for 'sacrific' returns exactly eight cards and not one is a sacrifice OUTLET: Fabled Passage, Prismatic Vista and Gemstone Mine sacrifice themselves as their own cost; Gadrak, Ganax and Goldspan Dragon only print the Treasure token's self-sacrifice reminder; Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon sacrifices itself to tutor; and Sneak Attack's end-step sacrifice is the price of its own effect, not a conversion the deck chooses to make. Nothing converts a permanent you already control into anything. The new finding is Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge, added in v1.0.2: it makes a Treasure per nontoken creature that died this turn, which is a fodder PAYOFF in a deck with no fodder and no way to kill its own creatures on purpose. Treasures are of course spent — the claim is about creatures and permanents as an engine cost, not about resources in general. Manufacturing a fodder stage to fill the table would misdescribe the deck.

lines.note: Fifteen Faerie Dragon tokens enter as one event, so Dragon Tempest triggers fifteen times and every trigger sees X = 17 (2 pre-existing Dragons + 15 tokens). 255 damage available at a single target; the 30-life seat dies to the second. Miirym copies none of the tokens. The arrow is a feed and not a coincidence: the tokens ARE what Tempest counts and what it triggers on.

Panharmonicon doubles Miirym, so one Lathliss cast becomes two nonlegendary 6/6 copies, and those entries pay Terror 36 across six instances of 6 — of which 24 is attributable to Miirym's two copies, the other 12 being the two wave-1 triggers on Lathliss's own entry, which Miirym did not cause. The feed is one-directional: Miirym makes the bodies whose entry Terror prices.

Panharmonicon doubles every trigger in the cascade because each is caused by a creature entering — Tempest's six instances read 4,4,5,5,5,5 for 28. It multiplies the payoff, not just the bodies, and 007 measures the counterfactual: without it the same board deals 20.

The deck's only checker-passed arrow that reaches a finisher. {R} puts Drakuseth in with haste; the attack trigger fires the same turn for 4+3+3 and it connects for 7, and all 17 stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice. The same stack refutes this arrow ever pointing at the commander.

CLAIM: a turn-one Sol Ring is what casts a three-mana reducer on turn two, which is the sequence the 'reducer + ramp' component prices at 0.463 assembled / 0.336 by turn six, mean turn 4.195. No stack covers it.

CLAIM: Dragonspeaker's {2} stacked on eminence's {1} takes {3}{G}{U}{R} Miirym to {G}{U}{R}. Stacks 002 and 007 verify the cascade Miirym runs and 007 rules on eminence reducing a different Dragon's cost, but neither pays for Miirym with a printed reducer, so the discount that would buy her is not what was checked.

CLAIM, and it replaces the same arrow drawn through Rapacious Dragon, which left the 99. A Treasure does not raise mean available mana — it covers the one nine-mana turn. Ganax mints one whenever it or another Dragon you control enters, tokens included, which is the only Treasure trigger in the fuel stage that fires on a Dragon ENTERING — Goldspan's needs an attack or a targeting, Old Gnawbone's needs combat damage, Atsushi's needs a death and Gadrak's needs a creature to have died. STATED LIMIT: meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled names Ganax, so the goldfish cannot spend this Treasure and no figure in this artifact measures the arrow.

CLAIM, and the direction is the point: this and the Lathliss/Breaching Dragonstorm arrow below are the two that run backwards from the engine into its own fuel. Miirym's copies are TOKEN Dragons, and Ganax reads 'Whenever Ganax or another Dragon you control enters', with no nontoken clause, so a token copy makes a Treasure where it makes no Miirym trigger. Panharmonicon would double it. Nothing has resolved this and it is exactly the kind of token-versus-nontoken question 001 and 002 both had to settle for other cards.

CLAIM: Lathliss makes a 5/5 red Dragon token per nontoken Dragon entering, and Breaching Dragonstorm returns to its owner's hand 'when a Dragon you control enters' — a token qualifies, so the conversion stage recharges the fuel stage's free-cast enchantment. Unresolved: whether one entry returning the enchantment mid-cascade forfeits later returns, and how the return interacts with a wave of simultaneous entries.

CLAIM, and the timing is the whole of it. Smaug's trigger is 'Whenever Smaug attacks', so it goes on the stack in declare-attackers and counts your Treasures on resolution — BEFORE the combat damage step, which is when Old Gnawbone makes any. Within one combat Gnawbone cannot feed the trigger. The arrow is real across turns, topped up by Smaug's own upkeep Treasure, and inside a second combat bought by Scourge of the Throne. verified_by IS DELIBERATELY NULL: Old Gnawbone does appear in three checker-passed stacks (003, 004, 006), but every one of those boards names cards this 99 no longer holds — Aggravated Assault, Savage Ventmaw, Wrathful Red Dragon — and none puts Gnawbone and Smaug on a board together, which is what this arrow claims.

CLAIM, stated narrowly because the obvious version is wrong: Atarka gives each attacking Dragon double strike, which doubles Drakuseth's 7 combat damage, and does NOT fire its attack trigger twice — that trigger fires once on declare. Nothing has resolved this.

CLAIM, and the newest structural arrow in the deck. Twinflame Tyrant: 'If a source you control would deal damage to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls, it deals double that damage instead.' Dragon Tempest's per-entry X is damage from a source you control, so on 002's board the twelve instances would read 128 rather than 64 and the two-seats-at-40 ceiling (64 < 72) would fall. No stack has run the cascade with a doubler on the board, and the goldfish does not measure this card as a multiplier at all.

CLAIM, narrower than the Twinflame one and deliberately so: Solphim doubles only NONCOMBAT damage to an opponent or their permanents. Terror's entry damage and Tempest's are noncombat, so both double; Drakuseth's 7 in the air and every point of Dragon combat damage do not. That is why Solphim belongs beside the entry kill and Twinflame Tyrant beside both kills.

CLAIM: Sarkhan's Triumph is one of three cards that can find a named Dragon (with Worldly Tutor and Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, filed in mana), and Miirym is the Dragon the conversion stage is thinnest without. Fetching is not a rules question anyone has checked here.

CLAIM: the protection component (0.673 assembled) exists to carry the conversion permanents through one sweeper, and the conversion stage's own printed defences are two and narrow: Miirym's ward {2}, and Solphim's {1}{R/P}{R/P} plus two discards for one indestructible counter on itself. No stack has tested a wrath against this board. Note what v1.0.2 narrowed: Lightning Greaves replaced three counterspells and answers targeted removal only, so this arrow now rests on four board-wide answers rather than seven.

map_disagreements.component: THE MAP'S CITY NAMES ARE DETERMINISTIC FALLBACKS
map_disagreements.why: Every region in deck_map.json still carries label: null, so the names engine-facts prints are generated from role composition rather than read by a cartographer — which is how a 13-card city holding five cost reducers, five protection spells and two damage doublers ends up called 'Insurance', and how the deck gets two cities called 'Mana' and 'Mana II'. Read the membership, which is measured; the disagreements below are about which cards sit together, not about what they are called.

map_disagreements.component: city-4 read as an engine part
map_disagreements.why: Thirty cards, 31.3% of the 96 entries, and it holds members of SIX of my seven stages: output 13, conversion 10, fuel 2, protection 2, ignition 2, wincon 1. It is not a stage, and it is not quite the Dragon city either — enumerated against oracle text and type lines, ELEVEN of the 30 mention Dragons nowhere: Chaos Warp, Deflecting Swat, Garruk's Uprising, Generous Gift, Panharmonicon, Radiant Destiny, Return of the Wildspeaker, Rishkar's Expertise, Sneak Attack, Swords to Plowshares and Temur Ascendancy. What the city actually collects is red-and-green permanents and spells that act on a board, which is why a payoff layer and a multiplier layer land in it together. Anyone reading this map as an engine diagram would conclude the deck has one enormous engine and six accessories.

map_disagreements.component: THE DAMAGE DOUBLERS (new in v1.0.2, and the disagreement that matters most)
map_disagreements.why: Solphim, Mayhem Dominus and Twinflame Tyrant are the two cards v1.0.2 added that change what the engine PRODUCES rather than what it costs, and the map files both in city-0 beside Teferi's Protection, Lightning Greaves and the cost reducers — while the third multiplier of the same kind, Atarka, files with the Dragons in city-4. The clustering is not wrong about the words: 'If a source you control would deal damage… it deals double that damage instead' is a conditional about your own stuff, which is what Heroic Intervention and Urza's Incubator also read as. It is wrong about the job. This part of the engine is invisible in card text, and the goldfish makes the same mistake independently — both doublers sit in THE COMBAT KILL's castable-DRAGON leg, counted as bodies, while its multiplier leg stays at two cards and thin.

map_disagreements.component: Protection held for the big turn
map_disagreements.why: Six declared cards across two cities, 5/1, and the scatter table says the same. The map files by the ANSWER each card gives: 'permanents you control gain hexproof' and an equipment file with the discounts, 'choose new targets' files with the Dragons. The deck does not care which answer it is — all six come out of the same held mana on the same turn for the same reason, and that is a property of the TURN, printed on none of them. Two more answers sit outside the component entirely: Cavern of Souls' uncounterable rider, filed in a mana city because the rest of the card is a land, and Thunderbreak Regent's 3-damage tax, filed with the Dragons because it is one.

Twelve cards, 5/4/3, and the widest scatter in the table. The split is by SHAPE, not function: the five mana creatures cluster with the Treasure Dragons in city-1 because they are creatures, the four rocks form city-5 on their own, and Farseek, Nature's Lore and Skyshroud Claim say 'search your library' so they file in city-3 beside Worldly Tutor and Enlightened Tutor, which cost you a card and look for a spell. This matters more on this deck than usual, because v1.0.2's whole change was replacing artifact acceleration with creature acceleration — the map records that as five cards moving from one city to another, and the engine records it as the ramp becoming vulnerable to a sweeper it was previously immune to.

map_disagreements.component: A Treasure source drawn (the map is right and my stages split it)
map_disagreements.why: All six declared Treasure sources sit in city-1 and the scatter table calls the component coherent — one of six that do. The disagreement runs the other way here: I split the group, filing Smaug the Magnificent under wincon because the Treasures it counts are the damage its attack trigger deals, so it is simultaneously the fuel and the thing the fuel is spent on. That is a limit of a one-card-one-stage model, not a fault in the clustering. Two more members are conditional in a way neither the map nor the component records: Atsushi's three Treasures are a DEATH trigger and Gadrak's are one per nontoken creature that died this turn, in a deck with no sacrifice outlet.

open_questions.question: Do Twinflame Tyrant and Solphim, Mayhem Dominus both apply to the same damage event — a Dragon Tempest or Terror of the Peaks trigger aimed at an opponent — for four times the printed damage, and if so, who chooses the order the two replacement effects apply in (CR 616.1)? Resolve on a board with one doubler, then both, and state the multiplier exactly.
open_questions.why_it_matters: These two cards are v1.0.2's addition to the engine and NOTHING in the deck's evidence touches them: they appear in no passing stack, in no candidate combo line, and in no goldfish leg that measures them as multipliers. If both apply, stack 002's board reads 256 rather than 64 and the ceiling that artifact records — 'what neither board can do is kill BOTH seats, since 64 < 72' — stops being a ceiling. That is the single largest unmeasured quantity in this model.

open_questions.question: Ganax, Astral Hunter under Miirym and Panharmonicon: does a TOKEN Dragon copy entering trigger Ganax's 'Whenever Ganax or another Dragon you control enters, create a Treasure token', and does Panharmonicon double that trigger? Resolve on stack 002's own board with Ganax added and state the Treasure count.
open_questions.why_it_matters: This is the only arrow in the model that runs backwards from conversion into fuel, and it turns on the same token-versus-nontoken distinction that 001 and 002 both had to settle for Miirym and Lathliss — where the answer went the other way, because those two cards say 'nontoken' and Ganax does not. It also decides whether the deck's biggest turn pays for the turn after it.

open_questions.question: Stack 001 kills every opponent on its board, but that board assumes Ancient Gold Dragon has already connected in combat, and its d20 needs 12 or better rather than the 15 the scenario fixes. Build the REACHABLE version of THE ENTRY KILL — one of Dragon Tempest / Terror of the Peaks / Scourge of Valkas, one widener, one nontoken Dragon cast — and resolve whether the cascade reaches three opponents at 40 or state the exact shortfall, as 002 does at 64 against 72. Do not let it assume Panharmonicon: 007 measured that board without it at 20 damage, which kills nobody.
open_questions.why_it_matters: Lethality against ONE seat at 40 is settled affirmatively by 007; against three it is not, and the frequency is not settled either. The damage leg is three cards and flagged thin, and the whole target reads 0.235 assembled / 0.150 by turn six at mean turn 4.977, so what a REACHABLE board does is the deck's central question and both declared kills still carry UNVERIFIED in their own titles.

open_questions.question: Hellkite Courser's enters-the-battlefield trigger, one domain and three sub-questions: does it put The Ur-Dragon onto the battlefield from the command zone, does the haste it grants make an attack legal that turn, and does the return to the command zone at the beginning of the next end step add nothing to the commander tax under CR 903.8?
open_questions.why_it_matters: An oracle scan of all 96 entries returns Hellkite Courser as the only card that puts a commander onto the battlefield from the command zone, and the goldfish casts the commander by turn six in only 0.329 of runs at median turn 7 — so this is the only route to the deck's largest payoff that beats turn seven. It also decides whether Flawless Maneuver and Deflecting Swat are free on the turn that matters.

open_questions.question: Scourge of the Throne, alone: does its 'attacks for the first time each turn' dethrone-conditioned trigger untap all attacking creatures and grant an additional combat phase, and is 'the player with the most life' re-evaluated in that second combat against life totals the first combat has already changed? Then, given a second combat, do Utvara Hellkite's per-attacking-Dragon token trigger, Thrakkus's power doubling and Atarka's double strike each fire again on the re-declared attackers?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only additional-combat card in the 99 by an oracle scan of all 96 entries, it appears in none of the four presentable passing stacks, and THE COMBAT KILL is declared at 0.243 assembled with nothing verified underneath it. Stacks 003 and 006 ARE checker-passed and do resolve repeated combats, but they run on Aggravated Assault — an activated ability with no once-per-turn clause, on boards this list can no longer make — so they say nothing about a trigger conditioned on attacking 'for the first time each turn', which cannot chain off itself.

open_questions.question: Re-run the goldfish with THE COMBAT KILL's multiplier leg widened from two cards to three (adding Twinflame Tyrant, whose doubling covers combat damage to an opponent) and report the assembled / by-turn-six / mean-turn deltas against the tracked 0.243 / 0.157 / 4.866. Report the counterfactual as a counterfactual; do not overwrite the tracked figures.
open_questions.why_it_matters: The leg is flagged thin at 2 and the model calls that thinness a finding. If a card already in the 99 belongs in the leg, the finding is smaller than the artifact says and a downstream diagnosis sized off 'thin at two' would be sized off a measurement error. It also tests whether the same card counted twice — it currently sits in the castable-Dragon leg of the same target — is a shared-leg violation of the kind this declaration has already been corrected for three times.

open_questions.question: Does anything in the current 99 make its own creatures die on purpose, and if not, what are Atsushi's death trigger and Gadrak's end-step Treasure trigger actually worth? Measure how often each fires in a seeded run rather than assuming they are dead text.
open_questions.why_it_matters: absent_stages declares fodder absent on a re-verified scan, and that is the right call — but two of the six declared Treasure sources are priced as if they fire freely, and both need a creature to die. The Treasure component reads 0.676 assembled on a DRAWN-cards question that cannot see this, and the mana it implies is already a floor because three of the six are unmodelled.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: A Treasure source drawn — six in the 99, of which the model can SPEND only two
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Relabel to name three, not two: 'A Treasure source drawn — six in the 99, of which the model can SPEND three'. Leave the six-card leg unchanged.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: The label states a figure that the file it is measured against contradicts. goldfish_metrics.json meta.treasure_sources_not_modelled names exactly three — Atsushi, the Blazing Sky, Gadrak, the Crown-Scourge, Ganax, Astral Hunter — leaving three of the six modelled, not two. The 'two' is carried from v1.0.0, when the unmodelled list was five. A label that misstates its own model is how a reader turns a floor into a ceiling.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: THE COMBAT KILL (UNVERIFIED — no passing stack): a Dragon-damage MULTIPLIER AND a Dragon to attack with
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Move Twinflame Tyrant from need[1] (the castable-Dragon leg) to need[0] (the multiplier leg), making the legs 3 and 7 rather than 2 and 8. Do not add it to both.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Twinflame Tyrant reads 'If a source you control would deal damage to an opponent or a permanent an opponent controls, it deals double that damage instead' — that is a Dragon-damage multiplier by the same test that put Atarka (double strike) and Thrakkus (double power) in the leg, and it is unconditional where Atarka needs an attack and Thrakkus needs to attack himself. It is currently counted as a BODY. Moving rather than adding is the point: this declaration has already been corrected three times for a card sitting in both legs of one target, where one drawn card satisfied both needs.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: THE ENTRY KILL (UNVERIFIED — no passing stack): a per-dragon DAMAGE payoff AND a way to put several Dragons on the battlefield at once
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Do NOT add Solphim or Twinflame Tyrant to the three-card damage leg. Declare a separate two-card component instead: 'DAMAGE DOUBLER drawn (v1.0.2's addition, measured nowhere) — Solphim, Mayhem Dominus, Twinflame Tyrant'.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: Both double damage and neither produces any, so putting them in a leg whose question is 'do I have a per-Dragon damage payoff' would let a doubler alone read as assembled — the exact defect corrected when Miirym and Lathliss were removed from this leg for being token makers rather than damage payoffs. Measuring them separately says what is true: the deck added two multipliers, they are thin at two, and no target currently counts them as multipliers at all.

proposed_goldfish_edits.target: Protection held for the big turn
proposed_goldfish_edits.change: Leave the six-card component alone. Consider recording in the target's own note what v1.0.2 traded: three counterspells out, Lightning Greaves in, and Greaves cannot answer a board wipe.
proposed_goldfish_edits.why: The rate did not move much (0.673 assembled) and the count is nearly the same, so the measurement looks stable while the COVERAGE narrowed — the component now holds four board-wide answers and two conditional ones where it held seven answers of which three could stop a sweeper on the stack. Adding Thunderbreak Regent to raise the count would be the wrong fix: it prices removal rather than preventing it, is never held up out of open mana, and the deck's own log (game 003, loss, cause 'politics') is the datum that the tax did not deter a converging table.
